items.title: The tracker is a separate repository with its own history
items.description: VOID-za/eje-tracker, outside the EJE checkout entirely, so that the EJE lint, typecheck and build never see tracker files and the tracker can never become a dependency of the EJE application.

items.title: The tracker database, its schema and its migrations
items.description: Its own database, its own role, plain numbered SQL migrations applied once and in order, one transaction per migration. Tables: items, history, relations, item_files, commits, releases, release_items, verification_runs, rules, decisions, users, sessions, audit_log.
items.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

items.title: The Rules model
items.description: Rules are first-class constraints in their own table: no DONE state, and nothing in the tracker can close one. Each carries its number where it has one, its wording, how authoritative that wording is, its source, source type and date, its last verified state, every other wording ever recorded for it, and its full history. The rule model is now final and both rule decisions are closed: rules 25-27 hold the owner's own words; rules 1-10 stay active on the recorded rendering (TRK-BD-02); rules 11-24 stay SOURCE_MISSING with the recovery record behind them (TRK-BD-01); and the 32 recovered standing rules stay under their own identifiers rather than being renumbered.
items.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

items.title: The task model: two axes, and a lifecycle that cannot be skipped
items.description: status (how far the work has got) and delivery (how far the code has got) are separate columns with separate vocabularies, and a status change goes through the lifecycle — OPEN cannot jump to DONE.
items.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

items.title: Decisions, with the question and the options kept after the answer
items.description: Every unresolved business decision in the scope is imported as an item of kind Decision plus a decision record. An unanswered question is DECISION_REQUIRED; an answered one keeps the original question and options beside the answer.
items.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

items.title: Audit findings stay visible until they are resolved

One administrator account, created on the server; the password is never in Git, in code, in a document, in a seed or in a log.

A rule marked SOURCE_MISSING now carries the evidence of the search behind it, and nobody needs to repeat the work.

items.description: Migration 0003 adds source_type (OWNER_MESSAGE, SCOPE_DOCUMENT, OWNER_RESTATEMENT, NONE, UNKNOWN) and source_date to rules, extends variant kinds with TASK_SCOPED and DESCRIPTION so the evidence about rules 1-10 can be recorded rather than described, and adds the append-only rule_searches table.

items.title: A decision closes when it is answered, not when something is built
items.description: Closing TRK-BD-01 and TRK-BD-02 needed a lifecycle edge the tracker did not have: an item waiting on a decision could not become DONE, which is exactly right for work and wrong for a decision record, where the recorded answer IS the deliverable. The edge DECISION_REQUIRED → DONE now exists for items of kind Decision only; for every other kind it is still refused, with a refusal that says why. Whatever an answer obliges anybody to build remains a separate item with its own lifecycle.
items.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT TRACKER — FINALIZE CONTROL LAYER AND PREPARE FOR EJE CONTINUATION", 26 September 2026

items.title: The shared control loop is documented and executable
items.description: docs/workflow.md records the loop the project owner asked for — human → ChatGPT → tracker → Claude → tracker — what Claude must read before EJE work and record after it, what DONE means, what is automatic and what is not, and the prompt preamble the owner can paste above any task. `npm run brief` prints the live state as one page (or --json), which is the read Claude performs and the text the owner pastes into ChatGPT.
items.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 4: LIVE TRACKER DEPLOYMENT + SHARED PROJECT CONTROL WORKFLOW", 26 September 2026

items.title: ChatGPT cannot reach the tracker directly, and that is documented
items.description: There is no ChatGPT → tracker integration and none was invented. ChatGPT cannot reach a service bound to 127.0.0.1:3100, and publishing the tracker to make it possible is a security decision the owner has not taken. The documented path needs no open port: the owner runs npm run brief and pastes one page, or reads the tracker over the SSH tunnel. The read-only JSON API serves anything that can reach the host.
items.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 4: LIVE TRACKER DEPLOYMENT + SHARED PROJECT CONTROL WORKFLOW", 26 September 2026

items.title: import:git rewrote four change requests on every run
items.description: Found by Phase 4's idempotency check, not by a test. A change request that names an implementing commit in its own dateline AND carries requirement rows was written twice per run: the commit pass said DEPLOYED, the roll-up said NOT_STARTED, and CR-01, CR-04, CR-07 and CR-09 oscillated forever, filing two history rows each every time. The roll-up now wins — a batch is only as delivered as its weakest part — and the commit pass skips any item that carries others. Second and third runs now report 0 delivery changes. Covered by a regression test that builds the exact shape and imports three times.
items.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 4: LIVE TRACKER DEPLOYMENT + SHARED PROJECT CONTROL WORKFLOW", 26 September 2026

items.title: Four dead links on the dashboard activity list
items.description: The dashboard linked every history entry to /items/<id>, including rule and import events, which have no item page — /items/git, /items/rules, /items/docs/SCOPE.md and /items/tracker-items all 404'd. A rule entry now links to its rule, an import event is plain text, and a test walks every link on every page and asserts each one answers. /commits, which Phase 4 asked to verify, now redirects to /releases where commits are shown, rather than rendering the same table a second time.
items.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 4: LIVE TRACKER DEPLOYMENT + SHARED PROJECT CONTROL WORKFLOW", 26 September 2026

items.title: A resolved audit finding read as an open acceptance blocker
items.description: CR-09 Phase 1 closed AUD-1 in docs/SCOPE.md with the word the scope uses for a finding — RESOLVED, because nobody "completes" a defect. statusFromScope knew DONE, SUPERSEDED, DEFINED, NOT IMPLEMENTED, PARTIAL, UNVERIFIED, BLOCKED, FAIL and OPEN, and fell through everything else to OPEN. So the brief went on listing AUD-1 as an open acceptance blocker after the scope had answered it. RESOLVED now maps to DONE, with a test on the exact wording the scope carries. The default stays OPEN: nothing said is still nothing claimed.
items.source: Found while importing the EJE scope after CR-09 Phase 1, 26 September 2026

items.title: A tested requirement awaiting approval read as untouched
items.description: IDEM-2 came back from the EJE work as "TESTED — awaiting approval", which is the honest state: implementation and tests are in, the owner's approval is not. statusFromScope had no branch for it, so it fell through to OPEN and the brief reported a requirement with 21 passing tests as untouched. TESTED now maps to TESTING, which is the step docs/workflow.md already puts between IMPLEMENTED and APPROVED. It deliberately does NOT map to DONE: that would claim the owner's approval, which is the one thing the tracker cannot check and the one claim it must never make on its own.
items.source: Found while importing the EJE scope after IDEM-2, 26 September 2026

decisions.title: Are the recovered founding principles the missing rules 11-24?
decisions.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026
decisions.question: Are the fourteen founding ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES (PRIN-01 to PRIN-14) the missing rules 11-24?
decisions.options:
(a) Map named recovered rules onto the numbers — say which rule is which number, and the tracker applies it with every record kept and the change written into each rule's history.
(b) Supply the wording of rules 11-24 from a source the tracker cannot reach (a ChatGPT conversation, a note, an email) and it is imported verbatim.
(c) Accept that rules 11-24 were never a distinct numbered set, close the gap by decision, and keep the thirty-two recovered rules as the unnumbered standing rules they are.
(d) Renumber the whole rule set deliberately, as a documented decision with a date - a new register, not a recovery.
decisions.decision: The original wording for Rules 11–24 could not be recovered from the available project sources. The missing numbers are retained as SOURCE_MISSING rather than being reconstructed or invented. Recovered scope principles remain separately recorded under their actual source/provenance.
decisions.implementation_status: Applied. RULE-11…RULE-24 keep empty text, status SOURCE_MISSING and wording authority MISSING, each carrying the record of the searches behind that conclusion. Nothing was renumbered: the 32 recovered standing rules stay under SCOPE-P*, SCOPE-D*, PRIN-* and STAND-01 with their own provenance.

decisions.title: Is the recorded wording of rules 1-10 the authoritative wording?
decisions.description:
THREE versions of rules 1-10 are now on record, all written by the project owner, none of them demonstrably the original:

A. Phase 2 §7, introduced as "The established rules include:" — the text the tracker records.
B. The BD-06 task preamble, "IMPORTANT PROJECT RULES" — whose rule 2 says "in this task".
C. Phase 3B §4, "The known wording currently recorded includes the following principles" — which differs from what is in fact recorded, most visibly at rule 2 ("Do not break existing functionality while implementing changes" against A's "Investigation/audit work must not silently modify application code, schema or data").

Phase 3B instructed that the recorded wording be preserved and not silently replaced, so A remains the recorded text and B and C are kept as variants against each rule. The rules are in force either way; it is their exact wording that is unsettled. Evidence that A is itself a restatement: A also carried rules 25-27, and the owner's authoritative wording for those three differs from A's version of them.

CLASSIFIED at the third search, on the evidence of how each version introduces itself: the Phase 2 §7 wording is register-framed ("The established rules include:") and is what the tracker records; the BD-06 version is TASK_SCOPED, because its own rule 2 says "in this task"; the Phase 3B §4 version is a DESCRIPTION, because it introduces itself as "the known wording currently recorded". That settles what each version IS. What it does not settle is whether the recorded text is the owner's original wording — the same Phase 2 list restated rules 25-27, and the owner's own wording for those differs from it. Only the owner can close that.

DECIDED 26 September 2026 by the project owner: the recorded rendering stays in force as the current wording, explicitly NOT declared to be the owner's original; the historical variants stay preserved and classified, and are never promoted to current rules.
decisions.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 3A: AUTHORITATIVE RULE RECOVERY + TRACKER DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION", 25 September 2026
decisions.question: Is the recorded wording of rules 1-10 the authoritative wording, or does the original exist elsewhere?
decisions.options:
(a) Confirm the recorded wording (A) as authoritative.
(b) Confirm the Phase 3B §4 wording (C) as authoritative — the tracker would record it as the rule text and keep A and B as variants.
(c) Supply the original wording from the authoritative project source, and it is imported verbatim.
(d) Restate rules 1-10 afresh — new rules with a new date, not a recovery.
decisions.decision: Rules 1–10 remain active using the currently recorded rendering because no stronger recoverable original wording was found. Historical variants remain preserved and are not treated as separate current rules.
decisions.implementation_status: Applied. RULE-01…RULE-10 stay ACTIVE with the recorded rendering and wording authority RENDERING — the tracker does not claim it is the owner's original. The BD-06 task-scoped version and the Phase 3B description remain as classified variants against each rule, not as rules. Rule 1 keeps its single variant: its Phase 3B wording was identical, and identical wording is not a second version.
